neighbours.label: a role noun naming a person by their relation to someone else, after a possessive ('his new boss', 'my teacher', 'his former masters')
fire: Every morning she brought coffee to her demanding boss.
He wrote a long letter to his former teacher.
Years later she met her old landlord at the market.
The farmer paid his workers at the end of every week.
I finally told my manager that I was leaving.
She trusted her lawyer more than her own family.
He still visits his childhood doctor once a year.
The knight bowed before his master and waited.
quiet: Every morning she brought coffee to her small office.
He wrote a long letter about his former school.
Years later she found her old bicycle in the barn.
The farmer paid his bills at the end of every week.
I finally told my story at the meeting.
She trusted her instincts more than her own memory.
He still visits his childhood home once a year.
The knight bowed before the altar and waited.
